_doc: RADE manifest (contract: rhope-ops/RADE schemas/rade-manifest.schema.json). Built by the RADE engine through scripts/build_paste_bundles.py (a pinned shim, see scripts/rade.lock.json). Each bundle is one round: a self-contained PowerShell text the PFM copies from its raw page and pastes into Windows PowerShell ISE (F5). It writes the files, then opens RADE, the Redacted Application Deployment Engine (a window; text prompts if no window can open): steps run one by one with a live log and PASS/FAIL counts, then one results folder (Rounds\\<round>: a report file plus copies of the PDFs, to attach to one e-mail; zips do not cross the boundary) and a summary for the clipboard. It runs only the steps inside it (PFM 3A). A step's "default" may be {passed, paths}: the step is ticked only when those files changed since the round that passed it; after a round passes it, set passed to the new hash (PFM 14 Nov 26). Never hand-edit scripts/gov/paste/*.ps1: change this file or the sources and rebuild. A step may list "needs" (check ids in the engine's $checkDefs) and "estimate" (minutes, used until a real run time exists). "apps" is the embedded catalog the Choose screen lists (name, plain-English summary, step names); without it, one application has every step. A guide step may set "doneText" (its Done button) and "doneLog" (the log line on Done).

steps.name: T22 Open the 90-161.Z window r8
steps.title: Open the 90-161.Z window and do its 18 checks
steps.note: Opens your 90-161.Z window with fake data and saves a picture of each card. Do each of the 18 checks in the bar at the bottom, then select Pass or Fail. Then close the window.
steps.help: Send the results as they are. The step can be run again.

steps.name: T22 Did the window open r8
steps.title: Check that the window opened
steps.note: Reads the result of the window step and opens nothing. Passes when the window opened, so the look questions run even when a check failed.
steps.help: Send the results as they are.
steps.doing: Reading the result of the window step.

steps.name: T22 Answer: look and cards r8
steps.title: Answer 3 questions about the window look
steps.note: 3 questions about the look of the window. About 2 minutes.
after: T22 Did the window open r8

answers.prompt: Does the window look like your vision of the 90-161.Z app?
Did every card open and fit with no scroll bar?
What would you change first? One line, no names.

steps.name: T21 Check the test site is clean r9
steps.title: Check that the last round left nothing on the test site
steps.note: Signs in (CAC). Removes a test list, library or Visitors member left by the last round. A test person still in PFM Office is reported as FAILED; the last step removes them.
steps.help: Send the results as they are. Each removal runs even when an earlier one fails.
steps.doing: Checking that the test site is clean.

steps.name: T21 Make the probe list r9
steps.title: Make the test list and library
steps.note: Signs in (CAC). Makes the fake probe list (Visitors get Contribute on this list only) and library, uploads one fake workbook and writes the test page.
steps.help: Send the results as they are. A second run changes nothing.
steps.doing: Making the test list and library.

steps.name: T20 Give PFM Office the edit-all level r3
steps.title: Check the lists and give PFM Office its level
steps.note: Signs in (CAC). Checks the 12 app lists: makes what is missing and puts the columns of its 18 views back. Then makes the group PFM Office and its level if missing, and reads them back.
steps.help: Send the results as they are. A second run changes nothing.
steps.doing: Giving PFM Office its permission level.

steps.name: T19 Set the 15-day suspense and the stage 6 target r5
steps.title: Set 15 business days and the stage 6 target
steps.note: Signs in (CAC). Sets the coordination suspense from 20 to 15 business days (DAFMAN 90-161 5.2) and the stage 6 target from 25 to 20. Other values stay and are reported.
steps.help: Send the results as they are.
steps.doing: Setting the suspense to 15 business days and the stage 6 target to 20.

steps.name: T21 Add the second person r9
steps.title: Add the second person to the test site
steps.note: A small window asks for the e-mail address of the second person. It stays on this computer. Adds that person to the site's Visitors group.
steps.help: Send the results as they are. The address is never written to a file; the results show only yes or no.
after: T21 Make the probe list r9
steps.doing: Adding the second person to the Visitors group.

steps.name: T21 Give the second person PFM Office r9
steps.title: Put the second person in PFM Office
steps.note: Signs in (CAC). Makes one test row as you, puts the second person in PFM Office for this round, checks that the person can now edit every row, and copies the link of your row.
steps.help: Send the results as they are.
after: T21 Add the second person r9
T20 Give PFM Office the edit-all level r3
steps.doing: Putting the second person in PFM Office.

steps.name: T21 Second person edits your row r9
steps.title: Ask the second person to change your row
steps.note: You need one person of your office for about 10 minutes. They open the link of your test row, type an X at the end of the Title and select Save.
guide: 1. Ask the second person to stay at a computer for about 10 minutes.
2. Open Teams.
3. Select "Chat".
4. Select "New chat".
5. In the box "To", type the e-mail address you gave RADE for the second person.
6. Select the chat box.
7. Press Ctrl+V (the link of your test row is on the clipboard).
8. In the chat box, type: Open this link, add an X to the Title, select Save, tell me if it saved.
9. Press Enter.
10. Wait for the reply: the row saved, or no permission.
If nobody can help now: select "Skip" (the test of the PFM Office level then stays open).
after: T21 Give the second person PFM Office r9

answers.prompt: What did the second person see?

steps.doneLog: Confirmed by you: the second person tried the row.

steps.name: T21 Power Automate shows your connections r9

guide: 1. Select "Open in browser" above.

3. On the left, select "Connections" (it can be under "More" or "Data").
4. Wait until the list of connections shows.
5. Look in the list for a SharePoint connection.
If the page says the connections could not be loaded: wait 5 minutes, then reload the page.
If the list still does not show after the reload: select "It failed".

steps.name: T24 Import the full solution r5: choose the file
steps.title: Start the import of the full flows
steps.note: You start the import of the full 90-161.Z flows (every flow On). The next step finishes it. About 4 minutes.
guide: 1. Select "Open in browser" above.
2. If Power Automate asks you to sign in: sign in with your CAC.
3. On the left, select "Solutions" (it can be under "More").
4. Select "Import solution".
5. Select "Browse".
6. Select the box "File name".
7. In the box "File name", press Ctrl+V (the file path is on the clipboard).
8. Select "Open".
9. Select "Next".
If the Open window closes before the file is chosen: select "Browse" again.
If the box "File name" is empty after Ctrl+V: press Ctrl+V again.
If you see an error: wait 5 minutes, reload the Power Automate page, and try 1 more time.
If the page refuses the file: select "It failed".
In the "It failed" box, type only the line that starts with "Error" (no time stamp or session ID).

steps.name: T24 Import the full solution r5: finish
steps.title: Finish the import of the full flows
steps.note: You finish the import of the full flows. It upgrades the flows of the last rounds, so a message or a banner that they were replaced is normal. About 5 minutes.
guide: 1. If the page says the solution already exists: select "Upgrade".
2. On the page "Connection References", select the arrow on the right of the first connection box.
3. Select your connection in the list.
4. In each other connection box on that page, select your connection too.
5. Select "Next".
6. If the box "1 Site URL" is empty: type the address you typed in the RADE box "Site address".
7. If the box "2 Alert e-mail" is empty: type your work e-mail address (the one you use in Outlook).
8. Select "Import".
9. Wait for the line "Successfully imported".
If you see "The original workflow definition has been deactivated and replaced": go on.
If that message shows a button: select the button "Done" on that message.
If "Import" stays gray: in each box that already shows text, press Ctrl+A, Ctrl+X, then Ctrl+V.
If a connection box has no connection: select "New connection" in that box.
If you selected "New connection": select "Create".
If a connection box has a "Refresh" button: select it.
If a sign-in window opens: sign in with your CAC.
If the import fails: select "Download log file".
If you see an error: wait 5 minutes, reload the Power Automate page, and try 1 more time.
If the log file is saved: select "It failed".
In the "It failed" box, type only the line that starts with "Error" (no time stamp or session ID).
